conditions: n nonnegative integer; r not equal to one; zeroth power interpreted as one.

evidence: Write S=1+r+...+r^n. Subtract rS from S to cancel all intermediate powers, obtaining (1-r)S=1-r^(n+1). Divide by 1-r, which is nonzero.

Reference cross-check of the standard identity: https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-2/pages/5-2-infinite-series. Checked 2026-11-27. Approval is a maintainer review candidate, not independent human certification.

conditions: Absolute value of real or complex r strictly less than one; zeroth power is one.

evidence: The finite identity gives S_n=(1-r^(n+1))/(1-r). Since |r|<1, r^(n+1) tends to zero, including for complex r. The denominator is nonzero and the limit is 1/(1-r).
